originalTitle: Alleged crime boss Daniel Kinahan’s return to Ireland ends global game of cat-and-mouse
summary: Kinahan built boxing empire while in exile in Dubai but now faces trial in Dublin charged with directing organised crime
content: A decade after escaping assassination and fleeing into exile, Daniel Kinahan is back in Ireland – but it is not the homecoming he wanted. The alleged leader of the Kinahan organised crime group was extradited from Dubai in an Irish government jet on Sunday and met by a huge security operation in Dublin, marking the end of a global game of cat and mouse with European, US and Gulf authorities. The 49-year-old landed at Casement aerodrome in Dublin on Sunday evening and was taken to the criminal courts of justice in central Dublin to be charged with directing organised crime. A judge told Kinahan that, because of the charge, an application for bail would have to be made to the high court. Kinahan said: “I understand. I think we know I won’t be getting bail, but thank you.” He was then taken 50 miles outside the city to his new home in Portlaoise prison. Tabloid headlines anticipated his return with glee. “Du-Bye!” said one. “Dan and Dusted,” said another. “Kin Air: He’s Coming Home,” said another. It is a moment long sought by law enforcement agencies that named Kinahan as a leader of a cartel said to control about a third of Europe’s cocaine supply, along with running criminal sidelines in firearms and racketeering. As the founder of the boxing management company MTK Global, the Dubliner was also an influential figure in sports and boasted of friendships with Tyson Fury and other champions. Kinahan has not been tried but is braced for conviction and a long sentence, according to clips of an interview that he gave by phone from Dubai to the podcaster James English. “I think I’ve already got life in prison. And we have to go through the dance now.” The married father of five said he had “not been an angel” but that accusations against him were overblown. “I believe in a way I’m a scapegoat.” He had not laundered money through boxing promotion, he said, rebutting one of the allegations against him. Kinahan said he looked forward to familiar Irish treats such as a crisp sandwich. “Get back home and have a little bit of batch bread and a packet of King crisps or Tayto.” The bravado, or fatalism, could not disguise a dramatic fall. From gilded opulence in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), allegedly at the helm of a criminal empire worth hundreds of millions of euros, Kinahan will reportedly become an inmate at the maximum-security A5 unit within A block at Portlaoise. His father, Christopher Kinahan, launched a family enterprise in the 1980s by importing heroin into Dublin. A polished figure with university degrees and a facility for languages, Kinahan senior, better known as Christy, was convicted of drug offences and money laundering while creating a network that spanned Latin America, north Africa, the UK and continental Europe. In 2009, a US diplomatic cable named his son Daniel as “an Irish businessman involved in narco-trafficking throughout Europe”. Soon after, Spanish authorities arrested Christy and Daniel and seized assets, but the Kinahans emerged largely unscathed. That changed when a murderous feud with the rival Hutch gang piled up corpses and led to an audacious but unsuccessful attempt on Daniel’s life at a boxing weigh-in at Dublin’s Regency hotel in February 2016. The death of one man, David Byrne, fuelled further killings. Kinahan was never again seen in public in Ireland and operated from southern Spain before settling in Dubai in the UAE, which had no extradition agreement with Ireland. With his father and brother Christopher junior, Daniel remained alert to surveillance attempts but lived openly and turned MTK Global into a boxing powerhouse. That apparent untouchability evaporated in 2022 when the US offered a reward of up to $15m for information that led to the arrest or conviction of the trio. Washington had been reluctant to get involved until lobbied by the then assistant garda commissioner John O’Driscoll, Greg Gatjanis, who ran the US national security council’s strategy for transnational organised crime, told the MacGill summer school last month. “To this day I hold Ireland, the gardaí, as the model [for international manhunts] of how they handled the Kinahan organisation,” said Gatjanis. “Their drug empire probably did not touch the US, but then he started talking about the effects of the Kinahan organisation and the terror they were inflicting. I went from telling him I couldn’t accommodate sanctions because I could not make a case for it to agreeing to starting up an investigation, and that began the entire sanction investigation.” In May 2025 Ireland agreed an extradition treaty with the UAE and the net began to close. Sean McGovern, a cartel lieutenant wanted for murder and directing organised crime, was extradited that month and jailed for 24 years. Daniel Kinahan was arrested in April this year. UAE authorities rejected his appeal last month, clearing the way for extradition. Irish military personnel are expected to reinforce police during Kinahan’s transfers to court and prison. Kinahan told the podcast he would be subject to a “circus” and “character assassination”. Gatjanis said no organised crime group lasted for ever. “It’s born, it crawls, walks, runs, starts to decline, ultimately dies.”
chineseTitle: 被指控的犯罪头目丹尼尔·基纳汉返回爱尔兰结束了全球猫捉老鼠的游戏
chineseSummary: 基纳汉在迪拜流亡期间建立了拳击帝国，但现在在都柏林面临审判，被控指挥有组织犯罪
chineseContent: 逃离暗杀并逃亡十年后，丹尼尔·基纳汉回到了爱尔兰，但这并不是他想要的回家。周日，这名被指控为基纳汉有组织犯罪集团头目的人乘坐爱尔兰政府飞机从迪拜被引渡，并在都柏林受到大规模安全行动的会见，这标志着与欧洲、美国和海湾当局的全球猫捉老鼠游戏的结束。这名 49 岁的男子于周日晚上降落在都柏林凯斯门特机场，并被带到都柏林市中心刑事法院，被指控指挥有组织犯罪。一名法官告诉基纳汉，由于这项指控，必须向高等法院申请保释。基纳汉说：“我明白。我想我们知道我不会获得保释，但谢谢你。”然后他被带到城外 50 英里外的波特劳伊斯监狱的新家。小报的头条新闻都欢呼雀跃地期待着他的回归。 “杜-再见！”一位说。 “丹和达斯德，”另一个人说。 “Kin Air：他回来了，”另一个人说。这是执法机构长期以来一直寻求的时刻，他们将基纳汉列为一个卡特尔的领导人，据称该卡特尔控制着欧洲约三分之一的可卡因供应，同时还从事枪支和敲诈勒索方面的犯罪副业。作为拳击管理公司MTK Global的创始人，都柏林人也是体育界的一位有影响力的人物，并与泰森·富里和其他冠军有着友谊。基纳汉尚未受审，但根据他在迪拜接受播客詹姆斯·英语 (James English) 电话采访的片段，他已准备好被定罪和判处长期徒刑。 “我想我已经被判终身监禁了。我们现在必须跳完舞。”这位五个孩子的已婚父亲表示，他“不是天使”，但对他的指控有些言过其实。 “我相信在某种程度上
